why: His case row carried no dates at all -- only the sentence text, Held on $40,000 bail. These are the custody dates supplied by the curator: arrested and incarcerated 30 September 1954, released November 1954.
sourcing: Supplied by the curator and recorded as such. A search turned up nothing that contradicts them and nothing that confirms the specific days either; the 1954 Smith Act membership-clause prosecution itself is well attested, the day-level detail is not something the public sources carry.
precision_note: The release is stored as 1954-11-01 with month precision, so the page renders November 1954 rather than asserting the first. The consequence worth knowing: imprisoned_for_days is computed from the stored date, so the duration comes out at 32 days, which is a floor. If he was released later in November the real figure is up to thirty days more. Storing the first of the month is the archive convention for a month-precision date -- the same as Audrey Hendricks in batch 206 -- and the precision flag is what stops the page claiming a day nobody claims.
not_touched: The sentence text, the empty institution and the released and in_custody flags are left alone. So are the birth and death dates from batch 223, which this batch prints back so a case write cannot quietly disturb them.
